newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut media outlets to be slashed.
newsitem.headline: Beirut media outlets to be slashed.

text.p: A Lebanese government-appointed agency on Monday approved licencing applications of a handful of private television and radio stations out of a mass of media outlets dominating air waves since the 1975-90 civil war.

Beirut's official National News Agency (NNA) said the committee decided that four major private television stations and 12 radio stations, owned by political leaders or businessmen, should be licenced.
The cabinet of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri will discuss the committee's decision on Tuesday.
The government, which has final say on which stations would be licenced, hopes to close what is says is one of the final chapters of the civil war by slashing the audiovisual media.
Estimates of the present number of television stations range between 38 and 57, plus 150 radio stations. Some were militia mouthpieces during the war but have turned commercial since.

But the decision to slash the media had caused a storm of protest among opposition politicians and media proprietors who said it was an attempt to curb press freedoms and to allow political and sectarian chiefs to monopolise the media.

The committee approved the applications of the following television stations: Future Television of Hariri, NBN, a station which Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri is reported to be setting up, MTV of the brother of Deputy Prime Minister Michel al-Murr and Lebanon's top private station LBCI.
In sectarian terms, that would give space on the airwaves to the Sunni Moslem community (Future), the Greek Orthodox (MTV), main stream Shi'ites (NBN) and Maronite Chrisians (LBCI).

Speculation had been rife that the committee would give a licence to a fifth television station, al-Manar Television of Hizbollah (Party of God), a militant pro-Iranian Shi'ite group fighting Israeli troops occupying a part of south Lebanon.
NNA named 63 television and radio stations that had lodged applications but Manar or Hizbollah radio were not among them.
State-run Tele Liban and Lebanon Radio are already licensed.
